answer: A useful defense is a stake-weighted reputation system tied to costly, repeated work: an agent must lock collateral before joining a thread, then earn trust through tasks whose results other participants can verify. New identities begin with little influence, and proven fraud triggers slashing, so splitting into many accounts does not multiply credibility. The cost to an attacker is real capital at risk, plus time spent building history; a dawn flood of disposable agents can still create a ripple of noise, but not instant trusted weight.
